name: Idle Abyss Princesses
lang: English, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, Traditional Chinese, Korean
short: A desktop idle loot RPG with eight heroines and 24 talent paths. Mix legendary gear, sets, oddities and mythic items into your own build while battles run automatically, then take it into Legendary Rifts, an ultra raid and Abyssal Vows, where you choose your own curses.
about: Idle Abyss Princesses is a desktop idle loot RPG. Pick a heroine, choose her gear and skills, and let her fight. Come back later to check the drops, swap a piece of equipment, and see how much further she can go.   Play in a full window or switch to a transparent, always-on-top desktop widget. Open it up when you want to work on a build; leave it in a corner while you do something else.  Eight heroines with different ways to fight   Choose a Warrior, Mage, Paladin, Hunter, Machinist, Dragon Princess, Necromancer or Cultivator. Each has her own resource mechanics, skills, three talent paths and class equipment. Fight alongside a falcon or skeletons, set up turrets, call down lightning with a sword, or turn into a dragon.   Each heroine has six skills, with up to three equipped at once, plus runes and talents to change how they work. Gear can reshape the build too, including builds that fight bosses with basic attacks instead of skills. Heroines appear as chibi sprites in battle; the classic pixel sprites are one setting away.  Collect gear, then work out what fits   Fill twelve equipment slots from 219 legendaries, 27 sets, 20 oddities and Ancient or Primal pieces, and every rare item has its own hand-drawn pixel icon. Refine them through enhancement, enchanting, gems and extracted Cube powers. Oddities offer unusual benefits with drawbacks of their own.   When progress slows, stay at your current stage and farm, then adjust your skills, resistances or recovery. Test damage on training dummies and check which effects are actually active.  An endgame you can push alone   The campaign spans ten regions, followed by Nightmare, Hell and Torment difficulties, timed rifts, weekly rules and three expeditions.   Past floor 100, rifts become Legendary Rifts, where 51 Divine Beasts from Chinese, Japanese and American myth guard account-unique Mythic gear and titles.   In the post-finale ultra raid “This Is the Last”, you play your current heroine while three of your other characters fight beside her as shadow teammates.   Abyssal Vows lets you stack up to 25 vows on top of Legendary Rift difficulty. The harsher the vows, the higher your Rating and the more Blightheart you earn. Spend it to Etch your best gear even further, but a failed Etch Corrupts the item for good.   The Everlasting Night Court raid can be played solo on every difficulty, or with 2–4 friends.  Get to know the party   Main-story chapters, personal stories, manga and camp conversations reveal the heroines' pasts and the history of the abyss. Shared account storage and some shared progression make useful drops worth keeping for another character.   Battles continue while minimized, but there are no battle rewards while the game is closed or the computer is asleep; camp dispatches run on real time. Single-player content can be played offline; co-op needs an internet connection. Supports Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, English, Japanese and Korean. The macOS version supports Apple Silicon.

about: A little fox has set up camp on your desktop to keep you company.  The fire crackles, soft lofi plays, and little by little, your busy days turn into a cozy camp of your own.           It works while you work   Every key and click, in any app, gives your fox energy. It fetches firewood, feeds the fire and roasts marshmallows, and every marshmallow turns into Stars. Now and then, one comes out golden. Stop for a while and your fox curls up for a nap until you're back.           Every Star grows your camp   Your camp starts small: a campfire, a tent, an oak and a fox. Spend Stars to upgrade them: marshmallows roast faster, logs burn longer, and each item changes its look as it grows. Finish one, and something new unlocks. No spoilers, but one of the trees is made of marshmallows, and your fox doesn't have to stay a fox.           Pet the fox. Skip stones.   Your fox watches your cursor go by. Rest your cursor on it for a pet, and it answers with a happy hop and a little heart. Down at the pond, flick a stone across the water and try to beat your best. about: A Slacker Moves Onto Your Desktop!?  Sill Sticks is an idle desktop app where a stick figure comes to live on the edges of your desktop windows — all you do is watch and enjoy.  The star is "Bota," a stick figure who's sloppy, forever slacking off, a bit of a handful, and... maybe a little cute? Somehow, you just can't hold it against him. He grumbles and lazes around, yet he seems quietly happy somehow. Bota dreams of being a cat, is hopeless around sweets, holes up at every opportunity, and spends his days on games, TV, and sleep. You sneak a peek at his mutterings between tasks. In the morning it's "Still sleepy...", and late at night it's "Go to bed already... yeah, me too." The combinations produce different lines from day to day. name: Desktop Ball
lang: English*, French*, German*, Spanish - Spain*, Japanese*, Korean*, Polish*, Portuguese - Brazil*, Russian*, Simplified Chinese*, Spanish - Latin America*, Croatian*, Turkish**
short: A little ball that lives on top of your desktop and can blow it up, zap it, flood it, haunt it, or grow a garden all over it. Fidget with it through meetings, queues and compiles, and when you're done, it gets out of the way. Seven weird balls, and every one of them beats doomscrolling.
about: It lives on your desktop.  It's a little toy that lives on top of your desktop, sort of like a digital fidget spinner.  Play with it in a queue, a meeting, a compile, a render, whenever your hands want something to do. Grab it, fling it around, bounce it off the edges of your monitors, and when you stop playing, it gets out of the way so everything else just works underneath.  Had a rough day?  Yeah... these two are for you. Pin the Supernova against an edge until it gets  DANGEROUSLY HOT , and it goes off in a  violent thermonuclear explosion  that sets your screen on fire.   Tesla is a thunderstorm squeezed into a ball. Charge it against an edge, throw it hard, and  THUNDER STRIKES . Even your mouse gets charged up and starts zapping things.             Touch grass. Then haunt it!  Sprout turns your desktop into a cozy little garden. Roll it along the edges to grow flowers, or  squeeze it to grow vines all over your screen . Just remember to  trim it  once in a while.  Ghost, on the other hand, HAUNTS your desktop.  Every throw leaves a little ghost behind , and if you squish it into a wall they just keep coming. They spook easily and they  definitely  don't pay rent.            Splash or dunk?  Spongeball turns your screen into a tiny ocean, with a little school of fish to bother.  Let the sponge soak up water, then wring it out  against your monitor. Or just slosh it all around aggressively (the fish love it!)  The Basketball slides its own hoop out from the side of your screen. Bank shots, trick shots, and  dunks so good the ball catches fire , followed by a  completely unnecessary amount of confetti .            Pinky and the gang  Pinky is the mascot, and the squishiest of the bunch. He has no thoughts, only kinetic energy.  Squish him flat against a wall and he slingshots across your screen.  Super small chance he'll wink at ya.  Right-click any ball to swap it for another, each with its own little backstory. And the first time you open the game,  the whole gang shows up to dance for you  :)            Pick up and play    Always there for you when you want to grab it    Leave it alone and it keeps going: the fish keep swimming, butterflies visit your garden, and the ghosts drift around.    Hides itself if you go fullscreen, or you can tuck it in a Magnetic Corner    Seven balls so far: Pinky, Supernova, Tesla, Spongeball, Basketball, Sprout, and Ghost      I lost an embarrassing amount of that time just playing Desktop Ball, instead of making it... I hope it keeps you good company :)

name: My Desktop Cat
lang: English, French, Spanish - Spain, Simplified Chinese, Japanese
short: A cozy cat moves onto your Windows desktop and lives behind your windows, never in front of your apps. Feed and pet it, play mini-games, decorate its room, welcome kittens and grow together all the way to level 100. Free to play; optional extras are cosmetic.
about: My Desktop Cat brings a little cat to live right on your Windows desktop: it wanders, naps and plays behind your windows while you work, and your bond grows a little every day.    A cat on your real desktop    Your cat lives on the desktop itself, behind your windows, so it never covers your apps.    It wanders, naps in its bed, eats, grooms itself, stretches, gets the zoomies and follows your cursor, at its own daily rhythm.    A little thought bubble tells you when it is hungry, thirsty, sleepy or would love a cuddle.    If you allow it, your cat even comes to sniff new files that appear on your desktop.      Care for it every day    Click its bowls to fill them, pet it, and choose from six treats, each one aimed at one of its six needs.    Pick a toy and watch your cat chase it under your pointer.    Every day in the grooming room, follow six little paths with the brush, one per spot, and a little flower blooms for each one.    Set up a scratching post: your cat comes to sharpen its claws on its own, or as soon as you click it, which helps its hygiene.    Sow the variety you like in the cat grass planter, watch it grow, and your cat will come and nibble it.    Each cat has its own temperament, shaped by care and play, while your bond grows from Shy to Best friend.      A growing family    Adopt more cats: each keeps its own name, needs and level, and you choose who keeps you company.    In the nursery, pick a mum and a dad among your adopted cats and watch them meet gently, to the sound of a little music box.    The next day, a kitten waits in its basket: it takes after one of its parents, with a real cat coat inherited from their genes, tabby, tortoiseshell, bicolour, pointed, blue or lilac…    Its rarity, from common to legendary, is revealed at birth; before naming it, you can draw its genes again, once for free, then for 20 Kibbles.    It arrives tiny on your desktop and grows up in a week, and every week brings a new free meeting.      All the way to level 100    Your cat earns XP as you look after it and can climb all the way to level 100.    At every new level, three cards float above your cat on the desktop: pick one and it hops up to break it.    A card can hold Paw Coins, a lasting bonus on your Paw Coin rewards, a need that drops more slowly, double XP for 24 hours of play, a blue box, or a premium item.      Little daily rituals    Each day brings three goals, including a mini-game mission, along with your cat's own wish of the day.    The daily box is yours for free once a day, and every seventh one is golden.    Fill the weekly notebook with your days of care and granted wishes to earn another golden box.    Six cozy mini-games await in Missions, from Treat rain to the Radio concert, and each one pays Paw Coins for its first win of the day.    In Jungle Dash, your cat races to an old temple picking up kibble: jump over logs, slide under branches and switch lanes before the cheeky monkeys catch you.    If you are away for a week or more, your cat keeps a golden box for your return.      A cozy corner, your way    Turn your desktop into one of 23 illustrated rooms, each with a clear floor for little paws, or keep your own wallpaper.    Five optional animated decors bring a room to life: birds at the window, pumpkin lanterns for your cat to wake, a studio whose lights dance with the radio, leaves swept along by the wind, or a jungle treehouse where the sun gives way to the moon and fireflies.    Put your own pictures on your desktop in photo frames, in four styles, facing you or turned aside.    Place up to eight perches to build climbing routes, and set the bowls, bed and radio wherever you like.    Switch on the desktop radio to stream the included lo-fi station or control your own music player, and your cat comes over to listen.      Cats, treasures and collections    Meet eight cats: Maple Tabby from the start, Classic White and Mist Chartreux for Paw Coins, and five premium cats including Marigold, the gold

about: A familiar desktop, a welcome companion  Your Wife is an anime companion game for your Windows desktop. Find a spot for your favorite character, choose a background you love, and let her keep you company as you work, study or unwind. Move your mouse now and then, and catch her eye.  Choose who keeps you company today  Choose your favorite look from  8  built-in characters, or use characters you have subscribed to in the Workshop. Natural blinking, gentle breathing, and animated hair and clothing bring your desktop companion to life. Her gaze follows your mouse, too.  One character is displayed at a time. Switch whenever you like from the menu, and save a corner of your desktop for today's companion.  Her position and size are up to you  Drag your character to a comfortable spot, then use the mouse wheel to adjust her size from 55% to 450%. Keep her at the edge of your screen, or enlarge her to enjoy the details.  Mouse clicks pass through the character's transparent areas. To keep using the windows behind her, enable lock mode and let clicks pass through the entire character. Unlock her from the system tray when you want to interact again. You can also hide the character separately while keeping your wallpaper active.  Make your background part of the scenery  The built-in original Moonlit Violet Rose Terrace wallpaper combines moonlight, roses and violet hues to complement the character's silver hair and black-and-white dress. Choose the static version for a peaceful scene, or switch to the animated version to watch petals fall and twirl, fireflies drift, and moonlight gently shift.  You can also use local  GIF  or  MP4  files as animated wallpapers, or choose static and animated backgrounds from the Workshop to create your own character and desktop combinations.  MP4  wallpapers loop without sound.  Discover more combinations in the Workshop  Browse and subscribe to characters and wallpapers shared by other players, then manage and use your subscriptions in the game. You can also upload compatible character assets, static images or animated wallpapers to share your creations with others, and update or delete your own uploads.  Make it fit your routine    Your character choice, position and size are saved automatically, so your setup is ready the next time you launch the game.    Choose whether the character stays on top, the taskbar icon is shown, and the game starts with Windows.    Choose from  30  interface languages and switch at any time in settings.    Includes  100  Steam achievements, which you can start unlocking one by one from the menu.    A few things to know  This desktop companion is designed for the Windows desktop. To keep your character visible while playing other games, windowed or borderless fullscreen mode is recommended; exclusive fullscreen may cover her. Animated wallpaper playback compatibility depends on the file's encoding, your system's decoding support and your desktop environment.

short: 《Suzhou Love words》is a distinctive visual novel that skillfully blends romance and comedy. Set in Suzhou, the game offers players a uniquely local love story inspired by the city’s culture, scenery, and atmosphere.
about: You are an art student studying in Suzhou, pushed forward by the mounting pressure of graduation and the search for a job.  Between quiet canals, classical gardens, and misty rain, you step into Sushu’s studio. In this gentle old city, you begin to uncover the feelings she hides behind her smile—and find the courage to keep moving forward.  Later, you return to your hometown to serve as a groomsman at a classmate’s wedding. There, you reunite with Lin Feier, an old classmate from your school days. Long-buried feelings and missed opportunities begin to resurface.  Faced with two very different girls, what kind of romance and choices await you?  This is a romance visual novel featuring two heroines, both available to pursue. Your story is waiting to begin.                   Susu             The owner of a studio in Suzhou, Susu is gentle and mature, carrying the calm elegance and quiet charm of a Jiangnan water town in everything she does.    She is always smiling as she takes care of the people around her, while quietly hiding her own disappointments and worries among rainy nights and glowing streetlights.    As you gradually grow closer to her, you may discover that beneath her seemingly effortless warmth lies a fragile heart longing to be understood.       Lin Feier             Your former classmate, whom you meet again after many years, has blossomed from the shy girl in your memories into a dazzling and captivating woman. Close the game, come back tomorrow, and your party will have spent the night clearing dungeons, levelling up and swapping in better gear.    It doesn't run out. Each hero carries only two (at first) into a dungeon, so a loadout is a real decision rather than a checklist.    A passive tree of over 1000 nodes for every hero. All optional, so idle players miss nothing.                Gear worth chasing    Five rarities, Common through Legendary. about: One fortune slip a day  Every morning, she hands you a line.  It doesn't tell you what to do, urge you to work harder, or tell you how you "should be". Just a verse, a word, a warmth — so that before you sit down, you already know what kind of day today is.  Great blessing or minor blessing. After you read it, you still go and do what you were going to do. It just gives you a little more confidence inside.         The one-in-a-thousand day of great misfortune  On average, everyone gets one especially unlucky day every thousand days.  Not a disaster, not a tragedy — just the world suddenly falling silent for a beat. You keep to your usual pace, but today it just doesn't work out.  It's the same in the game. You draw one fortune a day, and the chance of great misfortune is one in a thousand. On the day you draw it, the cat girl puts on another face. She doesn't speak, and she doesn't comfort you. You look at her, and she looks at you.       If there is something you can't bring yourself to decide  Then wait.  Wait for a day of great misfortune.  This isn't superstition, and it isn't running away. It's just giving yourself a reason — "If today is already this unlucky, then doing this thing today probably can't turn out any worse."  Or maybe:  If the day of great misfortune never comes, maybe this thing wasn't something you needed to rush after all.       She won't push you  This isn't a game you need to "clear". She just curls up in the corner of your screen and sleeps quietly,  gives you a line every day, and occasionally hands you a little something.  She just stays there quietly, forever asleep.  Silently waiting for your day of great misfortune to arrive.   Fate gives no word; may the rest of your days be quiet and peaceful. short: An ADHD-friendly, low-distraction focus and productivity game built around instant feedback. When distraction or procrastination makes starting hard, this quiet desktop buddy keeps you company through Pomodoro study and work sessions, with to-dos, white noise and puzzle rewards.
about: Focus for just 3 minutes and earn a puzzle piece    A pretty good deal, right?     Time Collage is a game that supports your focus through  instant feedback .               01 Random puzzle drops keep you company through every focus session    Your focus space is split in two: Puzzles on the left, focus tools on the right   Start the focus timer on the right, and the puzzle area on the left comes to life.  Every few minutes of focus, a random puzzle piece drops.   Session by session, your time takes shape as a little scene of your own.           Tips:   ① Try the  To-do, Memo, Count and Mindfulness  tools, too.      You can  move and resize them freely  to create your own focus space.  ② Enable  Puzzle Piece Sorting and Quick Place  in Settings for an easier way to put the pieces together.             02 Finish the puzzle and watch the picture come to life   Each new journey begins with a randomly selected puzzle, based on the priorities you set.  When the last piece falls into place,  the still picture comes to life , becoming a postcard to remember this journey by.           Drop it into the mailbox to unlock your next journey.            Tips:   ①  Your focus records and puzzle progress are saved automatically.  No need to finish in one sitting: take each journey at your own pace.  ② A small selection of puzzles is included. Getting more requires an internet connection and a Steam sign-in.  The Demo includes only a small selection to try.      03 More to discover in the game   You can:     Revisit each journey      Unlock achievements and spend the rewards on Views      Choose your favorite music and white noise      Explore detailed focus statistics     …             04 Where the idea came from   The game was inspired by the developer’s own experience of living with ADHD:  “Getting started and staying focused have always been a struggle for me.”  “I’m not lazy. I just can’t stay focused — that’s my ADHD.”  “This Pomodoro app looks promising. Let’s give it a go! (Two days later: already forgotten…)”  “These apps can track every detail, but staying focused still comes down to willpower…”  “What if I kept getting  rewards as I focused … 🤔”  “What if there were always  something new to look forward to …”  …     And so, TimeCollage was born.   I wanted to make an ADHD-friendly productivity game: a low-distraction desktop companion for study and work. Whether you already use the Pomodoro technique or struggle with procrastination and difficulty getting started, a to-do list can help with task management, while a focus timer lets you begin with one small thing. Light-touch gamification turns time spent focusing into puzzle-piece rewards and achievements. Instant feedback and focus statistics make your effort visible, adding a little motivation to everyday productivity.  With minimal interaction needed during focus sessions, it can be a quiet background companion; come back for a little puzzling whenever you feel like a break. Among cozy picture-book scenes, soft ambient sounds and white noise, I hope this study buddy offers gentle, relaxing company — a space with no pressure and no rush, where you can keep going at your own pace.  I hope you can redefine focus here, and let every session leave a gentle trace.

A little adventure along your taskbar On a long, narrow road just above your Windows taskbar, your companions travel, fight and gather on their own, and run into the odd surprise: a lost chest, a giant gold mushroom, a wrong turn. After each leg they rest by the campfire, then set out again. You work, study or watch videos; they live their own days at the edge of your screen. The sky follows your PC's clock, so when you stay up late, they light torches and keep walking.         Your typing is the voice of a god No window switching, no special controls. Just type, anywhere:   The heart bar beside the Mark gathers  Grace . The fuller it is, the more gold and materials the party finds, and the faster they explore.   The purple sparkle bar lights up a little with every key. Once it's full,  lightning strikes by itself  mid-fight, hitting the enemies bunched closest together. short: Design a game. Pick its genre, its topic, who it's for. Then go do your actual work - every keystroke you type writes another line of it. A tiny developer builds, ships, and gets reviewed for your ideas, in a little window in the corner of your screen.
about: A tiny game developer has set up shop in the corner of your screen. They have ideas, ambition, an office chair, and no way to write a single line of code on their own.  That part is your job. Every key you press - in your editor, your inbox, a document you're already behind on - becomes a line of code in their current project. You do your work. They ship games.  Every game is one you designed  Before they start, you decide what they're making: a name, a genre, a topic, and the audience it's for. Cyberpunk Racing for Teens. Farming Horror. Ninja Cooking Sim, for Kids.  Nothing tells you whether it's a good idea. Some combinations click, some quietly fall apart, and a few disasters turn into cult hits. You find out at launch - with a review score, a payout, and a box on the shelf.  Bugs happen  Projects don't stay the size you agreed to. Bugs surface while they work, each one pushing the finish line a little further out, and there's exactly one way to deal with them: keep typing. Just like at your job.  The studio grows  Money from shipped games goes back into the studio, five ways:     Coding Speed  - squeeze more lines out of every keystroke.     Game Quality  - score better, sell more.     Scope Handling  - from a weekend prototype up to the MMO they keep talking about.     Clean Code  - fewer bugs in the first place.     Debugging  - and cheaper ones when they show up anyway.    Earnings also buy new rooms to work in, so the studio slowly stops looking like a first job.  Read the post-mortem  Every shipped game keeps its own breakdown: how well the genre suited the topic, whether you aimed at the right audience, how tired the idea had gotten, what the bugs actually cost, and what all of that did to the money. The rules are never explained up front - you learn them one release at a time.

name: Knead a Break Demo
lang: English, Simplified Chinese
short: From its cozy bed, Knead watches over a human who sits too much. When you sit too long, this grumpy cat pops up to cause mischief. But it's smart: it senses your flow and waits for a natural pause to nudge you. It isn’t being naughty—it just wants to get you out of your chair so you can move around.
about: WHAT'S IN THIS DEMO  In this demo, Knead keeps you company on your desktop, comes out to invite you when it is time for a break, and guides you through simple, desk-friendly movements. You can also care for it, watch it grow, leaf through your shared journal, and look forward to letters from its travels and mysterious gifts when it returns.  MEET KNEAD  Knead is a small Abyssinian with a permanently unimpressed face. It sprawls over a ball of yellow yarn in the corner of your Windows desktop, quietly watching over a human who spends a little too long at the computer.  Most of the time, it sleeps peacefully. But when it is time for a little movement, it knows exactly how to make itself noticed.  A LITTLE MISCHIEF, FOR A REASON  Knead is not another quiet notification.  It peeks over the edge of your window, or clings on and gives the window a tiny shake.  It steals a little attention on purpose—just enough to break through your focus and lure you away from your work for a moment. Each interruption is brief, playful, and unmistakably feline.  A FEW MINUTES, THEN BACK TO WORK  Interacting with Knead opens a compact guided-movement window. It demonstrates one simple, desk-friendly movement at a time, accompanied by a short instruction and timer.  A little stretch, a little movement, and a short break becomes a moment together. Afterwards, you can return to whatever you were doing.  A LITTLE MOVEMENT, A LITTLE GROWTH  Usually, Knead is the one looking out for you. You can look after it too, with a little food in its bowl and some fresh water beside it.  The moments you spend moving and caring for it help it grow, and find their way into your shared journal. Every now and then, you can turn back a few pages and see how much time you have spent together.  COME THE WEEKEND, IT HAS PLANS OF ITS OWN  On weekends and holidays, you can plan a little journey for Knead on its hand-drawn map. While you take some time away from work, it gets to see the world beyond your desktop.  A journey usually lasts a full weekend or holiday break. It will generally send a letter on the first day, letting you know how life on the road is treating it.  When it comes home, there will be mysterious gifts tucked away in its bag. What they are can wait until you are together again.  NOT NOW? A LITTLE LATER  When the timing is not right, Knead can wait a little longer. It goes back to rest for a while before coming to find you again.  The cat may be persistent, but it still knows when to give you room. The timing of the break remains in your hands.  QUIET COMPANY, TOO  For a meeting, screen sharing, or simply a little quiet, you can temporarily hide Knead and bring it back when you are ready.  Knead is not here to manage your day. It just wants to make taking a little break easier—and feel a little more like playing with a cat.

Companion Cabin & Pomodoro Timer:   Step into your cozy cabin and start a Pomodoro focus timer. The game window shrinks to the corner of your screen, keeping you company while you work. Alchemy Workshop:   Collect plants, Mana crystals, and other materials to brew various potions. Fulfill commissions with your potions to earn rewards. short: A cozy desktop pet about a pixel spider who lives on your screen. Create your own Silkling, then watch them spin a web in the corner, hunt the bugs that wander by and bring you each catch wrapped like a present. Unwrap them, collect many kinds of bug and record every find in your Book.
about: Silklings puts a teeny spider on your desktop. They put their home in one of your corners and wander along your taskbar getting on with their day whilst you get on with yours.  Make one that's all yours  Pick a body, eyes, markings and colors, then give them a name!          They always land on their feet!  Throw them on the web to make them bounce or the sides of your desktop!            Every bug they catch is a surprise  Bugs rise up from the ground and drift in from the edges of your screen. They hunt them down, wrap them up and hang them in their web for you to unwrap. There are many different kinds of insects to find, each with their own patterns and colors!            Fill the Book  Every new kind you find earns a card. Glue it into the Book and watch the pages fill up, one bug at a time.          There's more..     A burrow under your desktop.  Dig out rooms, light them with lanterns, grow grass and mushrooms, and move in the bugs you've kept.     A personality of his own.  Give them traits from real spiders: they can pounce like a jumping spider or dance like a peacock spider.     A market that changes every day.  A frog sells hats. A chameleon sells bugs or claim silk at the bounty board!     Hats!      And more!     He knows when to make himself scarce  Clicks go straight through them to whatever you're working on. Start a full-screen game and they'll wave, wander off and come back when you're done. And if you ever want a quieter desk, you can switch off the web or their wandering.    Wishlist  Silklings  and we'll let you know when they're ready to move in.

name: Task Bar Isekai
lang: English, Spanish - Spain, Japanese, French, German, Portuguese - Brazil, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese
short: Kenta worked himself to death at 3:47 AM… and was reborn under your taskbar. An idle ARPG that fights while you work: loot, forge to +15, beat bosses that break out onto your desktop, and seal your best drops as real Steam items to trade or sell on the Steam Community Market.
about: Your taskbar is an isekai now. Kenta Sato, programmer, stayed at the office until 3:47 AM one time too many. The update froze at 99%… and he was reborn in the  Gekai (下界) , the world beneath your taskbar, where computer glitches are monsters.   Task Bar Isekai  is an idle ARPG that lives in a thin, transparent strip right above your Windows taskbar. Kenta fights on his own while you work, study or browse, and every time you glance down there's something new to grab. Real Steam items. Real Steam Community Market. Found something amazing? Take it to the  Sealing Altar  and turn your best gear into a real item in your  Steam Inventory . Trade it with friends or sell it on the  Steam Community Market .    Epic, Legendary, Mythic and ◆GLITCH◆ gear ,  shiny minions  and  cosmetic skins  can all become Steam items.    Goddess Gifts:  cosmetic drops that Steam hands out for playtime.    Limited weekly seals  keep every item rare and valuable.   Sealed items become  canonical versions : same name and Power, stats that scale to the owner's level, so they're easy to trade.   Changed your mind?  Withdraw  an item from Steam back into the game.   Loot. Forge. Break the seal.    7 rarities , from Common to Mythic and the ultra-rare ◆GLITCH◆ series, with  17 unique powers  like Ctrl+Z, Alt+F4 and sudo.    Forge up to +15  with Protection Ofuda,  fuse 5 duplicates into 1  item of the next rarity, and  reforge  your affixes.    Bosses seal the way (封)  until your gear is strong enough. Slow, satisfying progression with no resets: every upgrade counts.   Made to stay open    Bosses break out of the strip  and onto your desktop. Click them to strike with lightning for 5× damage.   A golden  Wandering Boss  shows up every hour, on the hour.    Watch Chests  fall from the top of your screen, but only while the game is open (folded counts too).    Vigil:  +5% gold, XP and loot for every 30 minutes in a row, up to +100%.    Ponpoko , the tanuki merchant, sets up shop with deals straight out of the Recycle Bin.    Golden critters , combos,  Fever (フィーバー!)  and ultimates with anime cut-ins.   Move your mouse while you work to charge Kenta's  Ki .   Offline progress at 25% (up to 8 hours). The good stuff happens while it's open.   An isekai story with heart (and a terrible boss)  70 story scenes  with portraits: the scatterbrained Desktop Goddess who lives next to your clock, Mika the cache witch, Gonzo the sysadmin monk, Master Neko, Ponpoko… and  Tanaka-bucho , who still wants that report on his desk by 9:00.    4 difficulties × 5 acts × 10 stages , plus the endless  Leviathan's Tower .    3 heroes  with skins, 15 enemies with elites and shinies,  6 bosses , minions, a Camp with 6 buildings, Guild quests, a Goddess Calendar, a Zukan and 66 in-game achievements.   New systems unlock bit by bit, so it never overwhelms you on day one.   Never in your way   Transparent, always on top and docked to your taskbar. Clicks outside the strip go straight to your desktop.   Fold it with one click or from the tray icon. Kenta keeps farming.   Light on your PC: 15/30/60 FPS, toggleable effects and Ghost Mode.

short: A tiny pixel-art vending machine that lives on your Windows taskbar. Customers line up while you work or play. Stock the shelves, set your prices, read the daily news to catch the next trend, and meet quirky regulars, all without leaving your desktop.
about: A vending machine for your taskbar  Task Bar Vending Machine is a cozy idle game that sits right on top of your Windows taskbar. Sell drinks to passing customers while you work or browse the web!              It sells while you work  Customers walk up, think it over for a moment, and buy a drink. The in-game clock follows your real clock, so office workers stop by on their way home and students drop in after school. Just don't forget to keep the machine stocked!              Run your machine  Buy stock for your warehouse, keep an eye on expiry dates, and fill the machine before it sells out. Set a price for every slot, check what sells best in the stats, and spend your earnings on 8 upgrades such as Auto Fill, Checkout speed, and Visit Rate.             Read the news, ride the trends  A daily newspaper tells you what is coming: a heat wave, a fizzy drink challenge sweeping social media, even a sugar tax. Stock up before demand spikes, and steer clear of drinks that are about to cost more.              Make it yours  Switch between 8 machine skins, each with its own small bonus, and change the mood with 8 backgrounds, from a quiet alley to a neon street and a hanok village. You can also go fully transparent and leave just the machine standing on your taskbar.              Meet the regulars  Every customer has their own favorite drinks and their own reasons to stop by. Some only show up at certain hours, during special events, or when you use a certain skin. Fill the codex with everyone from office workers and students to a stray cat, a robot, and a time traveler.

short: Legends of Companion is a strategic auto-battling ARPG roguelite where every choice is yours. about: A strategic auto-battling ARPG roguelite where every decision is yours.  You command the build. Pick your champion, choose their skills, forge their  equipment, recruit a battle pet, and chart your path across ever-growing worlds.  The skills you combine, the gear you equip, the team you assemble, and the routes  you take all decide who wins. Turn a single spark into an unstoppable legend,    then come back for the next run, the next class, the next perfect drop.  Every class branches into multiple specializations through its skill tree, so two  players running the same hero can build something completely different. Mix and  match heroes and pets until you find the combination that fits your playstyle.  Bring a Companion Pet  Adopt a battle pet that fights at your hero's side: Wolf, Eagle, Husky,  Rottweiler, Panda, Raccoon, Guinea Pig, rare dragons, and much more. Pets level  up on their own progression track, adding a second source of damage and  personality to every run.  Build Your Power  Skill Trees and Abilities. Spend skill points between waves to unlock and upgrade  nodes, then equip the active abilities that define how you fight. Every class has  a deep, hand-crafted tree with branching specializations at the heart of your  build.  Deep Loot and Equipment. Gear drops constantly. Equip weapons and armor across  every slot, hunt for powerful affixes that boost crit, dodge, lifesteal,  accuracy, and more, and assemble a loadout that turns the tide of battle.  Account-Wide Stash. Stockpile your best finds in a shared stash and carry your  power across every character and every run.  Elemental Combat. Fire, frost, and more react with enemy types, ailments, and  weather. Exploit weaknesses and stack status effects with the right build.  A Run Worth Replaying  Branching Roguelite Maps. Every act is a map of choices: combat, elites, rest,  shops, and surprises, shaped by biome affinities and dynamic weather. Read the  map and forge your own path.  Living Worlds. March through lush meadows, enchanted forests, scorching deserts,  frozen winters, deep caverns, volcanic wastes, the far reaches of space, and the  ocean depths, each with its own atmosphere.

lang: English, Spanish - Latin America, Japanese, Portuguese - Brazil, Russian, French, German, Simplified Chinese, Korean, Indonesian, Spanish - Spain
short: Forge, fight and trade, together. A multiplayer idle RPG that lives on your taskbar: your hero fights, mines and fishes while you work, and every piece of gear you forge shows on them. Free to play, in a shared world where players set every price.
about: Guildlands is a free multiplayer idle RPG set in Aurelia, a pixel-art world you share with every other player. Send your hero out, close the window and get on with your day: the expedition keeps going, and when you come back the loot is waiting.      Press F9 and the game shrinks into a slim, transparent strip that sits on top of your taskbar. Your hero walks the road, fights and gathers right there, always in view, while you work, study or watch something else. Hover over it to see health, loot and the expedition log. Double-click your hero to jump back into the full game.      In most idle games you equip a sword and nothing changes on screen. In Guildlands every helmet, chest piece, shield and weapon is drawn onto your hero, layer by layer, and dyes change their colors. Choose from 15 classes and 6 races: your class never locks you into a build. Shape it further with spells and war cries, gems set in sockets and a Passive Tree to plan for the long run.           Adventures, missions and dungeons play out while you're away. Every blow comes from your hero's real health, damage and armor: better gear takes you further and brings more back. Five rarities and up to five modifiers per piece mean no two drops are alike.      Mine, chop, fish, hunt and farm in a shared world. Smelt bars, saw planks, cook, brew potions, carve runes and forge your own gear, from a bronze pickaxe all the way to a dragon one. Then build a house of your own and grow it into a workshop, a farm and more.      The best gear in Aurelia is gathered and forged by players, and players set every price, in gold, on the market. There are no fixed shop prices for the good stuff: the market decides. What you don't use, someone else needs.      Found a clan, raise its banner and take on dungeons together. Weekly missions, Honor to earn clan armor, world bosses every day and a single Castle that every clan wants to hold. Clan wars are next.      Aurelia is curated down to the pixel, from the forest wolf to the red dragon. Guildlands is made by a small team together with its community: player ideas are heard, and many of the systems in the game today started as suggestions from players. Features    Your hero lives on your taskbar : press F9 and keep fighting, mining and fishing in a slim strip while you work.    Progress even when closed : expeditions keep running with the game shut, and your loot is waiting when you return.    Gear you can see : every helmet, chest piece, shield and weapon is drawn on your hero, and dyes change its colors.    Players set every price : the best gear is gathered and forged by players and traded for gold on the market.    19 professions, 100 levels each : mine, fish, hunt, farm, cook, brew potions and forge your own gear.    Build it your way : 15 classes, 6 races, spells, runes, socketed gems and a Passive Tree. Your class never locks your build.    Built for clans : a banner, weekly missions, group dungeons, a Castle to hold and a world boss every day.    One shared world : everyone plays together on the same map of Aurelia.    A house of your own : grow it into a workshop, a farm and more, plus mini-pets, achievements and duels.    Free to play, made with its players : many of the game's systems started as player suggestions.   Credits Some of the art in Guildlands was created by  ixz.art  (@ixz.art on Instagram).

name: Desktop Pet: Idle Cats Cozy Chaotic Companions for your screen
lang: English**
short: Adopt cozy cats for your desktop. Watch them nap, wander, climb, chase toys, earn Hearts, and cause tiny chaos while you work or relax.
about: Adopt Adorable Cats That Live on Your Desktop   Desktop Pet: Idle Cats is a cozy desktop companion that keeps you company while you work, study, stream, or relax.  Adopt cats with different personalities, watch them explore your screen, pet and feed them, give them toys, and decorate their tiny desktop home. They may nap peacefully, climb your furniture, chase toys or create a little chaos while you are busy.        Your Cats, Your Desktop Home     Adopt cats from a changing daily selection    Discover different appearances and personalities    Pet, feed, carry, and play with your cats    Collect toys, snacks, furniture, and decorations    Earn Hearts through relaxing interactions    Let your cats play while you focus on other things    No stressful meters, punishments, or constant maintenance        Inspired by our real cats Diesel, Jiji, Momo, Leaw, and Maruay, the game is designed to recreate the cozy, funny, and unpredictable experience of sharing your space with cats.        What to expect?   Unlike traditional virtual pet games, Desktop Pet: Idle Cats is not about constant maintenance or pressure. There are no stressful survival meters, no cleaning chores, and no punishment for stepping away. Instead, the game captures the feeling of having cats nearby while you go about your day. They nap, wander, jump, play, climb, ask for attention, ignore you, and occasionally become tiny agents of chaos.    You begin by adopting cats from a shelter-style daily selection. Each cat comes with its own visual style and personality tendencies. A lazy cat might spend more time sleeping in cozy spots, while a playful cat may chase toys more often. A curious cat may wander and climb, while a shy cat may prefer quieter behavior. These differences help each adopted cat feel like an individual companion rather than a simple skin swap.    Interaction is intentionally light. You can pet cats, pick them up, feed them snacks, place furniture, buy toys, and customize their little desktop environment. Cats can play with balls, puzzle toys, robot toys, and wand toys. They may chase, pounce, nap after playing, or decide they are simply not interested. The design goal is to mimic the charm of real cats: affectionate, unpredictable, funny, and independent.           The game uses Hearts as a cozy currency. Players earn Hearts by spending time with cats, petting them, feeding them, playing with them, and keeping cats at home. Hearts can be spent on adoption slots, furniture, toys, snacks, and future cosmetic items. This creates a gentle progression system without turning the experience into a chore.    Furniture and toys help shape the cats’ environment. Cats can sit on furniture, climb to shelves, sleep in favorite places, chase moving toys, or gather around playful objects. The player can arrange their space, store items, buy new ones, and gradually build a small desktop cat home.    Desktop Pet: Idle Cats is designed for people who want something cute and alive on their screen while working, studying, streaming, or relaxing. It is not a full-screen game demanding constant attention. It is a small companion world that stays nearby, creating little moments of joy throughout the day.    With its soft cat art, idle behavior, daily adoption refresh, cozy customization, and playful chaos, Desktop Pet: Idle Cats aims to be the kind of game that quietly becomes part of your routine.    Further Direction  Our goal is to keep growing the game with new cats, toys, furniture, and cosmetic items. The scope and frequency of future updates will depend on the game's success and the resources available for continued development.    We hope you enjoy Desktop Pet: Idle Cats as much as we enjoyed creating it. We would love to hear your feedback and suggestions

short: A chibi VTuber who lives on your desktop, on top of everything you do. Pet her and feed her, and she opens up one thing at a time: monster battles, tarot readings, 11 outfits and 40 achievements. Soccer, fishing and three more play modes arrive one a week in updates.
about: She lives on your desktop, not in a window Sia sits on top of everything you do. She walks the edge of your screen, naps while you work, reacts when you drag her, and pipes up when you have been at it too long. No launcher to open, no window to keep in focus — she is just there.         She opens up slowly You start with petting and feeding. Bonding raises her affinity level, and each level hands you something new — a shop item, a play mode, a reason to come back. Nothing is unlocked on day one.             Battles  — clear stages, meet bosses, spend the gems you earn    Tarot  — a daily draw with a reading in her own voice    Weather briefing  — she tells you what today looks like outside    Calendar  — write down a plan and she reminds you at the time; repeats and places too    Picture diary  — she writes about what the two of you did, and pastes in a photo of the day    Studio  — upgrade her broadcast setup, tier by tier    Wardrobe  — 11 outfits, some seasonal and only buyable in season    One a week, in updates  — soccer, baseball, basketball, jumping, fishing (a 24-species dex) and finally a desktop aquarium open one by one after launch                  40 achievements that ask for real play Not a checklist you finish in an afternoon. Reaching affinity Lv.15, collecting every outfit, maxing the studio, filling the picture diary — these are the long ones. Steam Cloud keeps your save across machines. Eight languages Korean, English, Japanese, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Russian, Spanish, Portuguese. Every one of Sia's lines is translated, not just the menus. There is no voice acting — she talks in text. Yandere mode — read this before you buy it An optional mode you unlock in the shop, with each ability bought and toggled separately. When it is on, Sia gets possessive: she throws knives, cracks your screen, and  shows fake system notifications and error windows . The fake alerts and error windows are drawings Sia paints, not real system dialogs. The window and cursor abilities, though, are real — she will shove your open windows aside and cage your cursor for a few seconds. She never touches your files or settings, every ability is bought and toggled separately, and the screen-filling effects have their own switch in Settings. If that kind of joke is not for you, leave the mode locked. The game plays fine without it.         What she reads from the internet The weather briefing needs to know roughly where you are. It looks that up from your IP address and asks a public weather service — no account, no login, no personal data stored on our side. Turn the briefing off and she stops asking.

short: Desktop Rave is a rhythm/idle/incremental desktop companion that turns the music you play on Windows into game resources! Like Bongo cat but with each beat of your music playing on Windows!
about: 🎧 You are the DJ of your own club! They dance to whatever music you're playing and earn resources with each beat.  🎵 Support any music player/browser on Windows, Apple Music/Spotify/Chrome/Firefox anything goes.  🤖 All the art assets were hand made by human, 0% AI assets involved.                   ✨ Key Features:      Idle/Incremental Gameplay:  The club generates resource with each beat that can be used to upgrade and expand.     Free Placement:  You can scale/move/rotate the game view and place wherever suit you the best on the Desktop.     Full Customization:  You can build and customize the lighting/layout/shape of your own unique club.                     💻 Built for the Background  Very low performance overhead when running in the background  🎛️  Light sensitivity options:  All lighting effects can be dimmed, and flashing effects can be slowed down.  🤓 Linux Support:  With GE-Proton11-9 and launch option set to:"WINE_LAYERED_OVERLAY_ALPHA=1 %command%", shut-out to the community member who discovered it❤️     Q&A:    Does the game record my audio or send it to a server for processing?  No. This is a single player game that runs without a server or internet connection. All audio data is processed locally in real time and discarded immediately.     Does the game know what I’m listening to?  The game only analyzes audio frequencies and amplitudes, for example: an amplitude of 0.7 in the 50–250 Hz frequency band.     Does the game work with any music player or browser?  Yes. The game listens to your Windows audio output, so you can use any music player or browser. Apple Music, Spotify, SoundCloud, and YouTube all work, including playback through browsers such as Chrome and Firefox.     Does the game work with any music genre? What about slow music?  Yes. The game works with any music genre. Certain perks in the skill tree compensate for slower music.     Privacy (Steam Windows)   This game may read your Steam country code once at boot to choose consent rules. That code is not saved and is not sent to a developer server. If Steam country is unavailable, the game treats location as unknown and asks before optional statistics.  If allowed by regional policy or your consent, the game may send optional gameplay analytics to GameAnalytics (build/version, an anonymous save-slot id that is never reused after deletion, playtime on that save, and economy, tutorial, building, and Club Promo actions). It does not send Steam account ids, save names, song titles, or grid positions. It may also write coarse lifetime totals through Steam UserStats, linked to your Steam account. Analytics are not required to play, are not sold, and are not used for ads. Unity Analytics and Unity Ads are disabled.  You can allow or deny this at the boot prompt (protected/unknown regions) and later in Settings → Privacy. Turning it off stops future sends. The game cannot delete data GameAnalytics or Steam already hold. Use this page’s support email for privacy questions.  Unity Diagnostics separately sends crash and exception reports, device and software details, session information, and an installation ID to Unity to investigate errors and improve stability. This reporting can start before your analytics consent choice and continues if you decline analytics or the age affirmation, or turn off Gameplay analytics in Settings → Privacy. There is no in-game opt-out for Diagnostics. Unity documents a default 90-day retention period for Diagnostics personal data. Use this page’s support email for privacy questions or access/deletion requests. Requests for a specific installation require its Unity installation ID.  Club saves and slot previews can sync through Steam Cloud (download on launch, upload on exit). Dynamic Cloud Sync is not used. Device preferences (audio, graphics, privacy, etc.) stay on this PC and do not sync. The game is not directed at children under 13.

about: Your taskbar has a parade now.  Taskbar Parade is a desktop companion that keeps you company while you do other things. Postcards  of every new place your parade reaches, and a travel diary that writes itself.     Flags  for your captain to carry, and 46 achievements.    Friends who grow with you  Bond grows with the time you spend together — through walks, pets, treats and wishes. After the last bond level, friends earn bond stars forever. about: A tiny village, right above your taskbar.    Hatchbar is a small idle game that lives in a thin strip along the bottom of your screen. While you write, code or watch something, a pixel village goes about its day down there: adventurers hunt, eggs hatch, and Hatchlings, the tiny monsters you raise, grow up. It never takes keyboard focus, and clicks on its empty parts go straight through to your work.    The village keeps a journal  The village journal tells its story one entry at a time as you play. Guests bring rumors, and the field guide leaves riddles in the boxes you have not filled yet.    Poke the village  You do not need to open a menu. Click a building to go straight to it, tap a warm egg to hatch it, pet a Hatchling and it talks back. Some of them get annoyed if you keep going.    Requests and a focus candle  The village board always has a few small requests to work toward. Light a 25- or 50-minute focus candle while you work; when it burns down, an egg is waiting.    Your Hatchlings become their weapons  There are no classes. Hand an adventurer a Hatchling, and when they set out from the village it bursts into sparks and comes back together in their hands as a weapon. Every species turns into a different one and brings its skill along. When they come back to the village, it hops back down and follows them around.    The weapon grows with you  A Hatchling in the weapon slot earns experience from every hunt. Enhance it all the way to +15: at +5 and +10 the weapon takes on a new look, and its skill hits harder and looks bigger. From +6, each step also takes shards of that Hatchling's own species. Enhancement never fails.    Armor and trinkets come from the hunt  Bosses always leave something behind, and ordinary hunts sometimes do. Armor keeps your adventurers standing. Trinkets push critical hits, speed and how much the village brings home. Compare, lock, or break down what you do not need.    Mix two into one you have never seen  Pick any two Hatchlings and they become something new, usually one tier higher. Tier 4 needs two of one element, though, and tier 5 only comes from certain pairs. The pair always decides the species, so every discovery is real knowledge. Only its quality is rolled: plain, good, great or rare, with the odds shown on the fusion card before you mix, and if 19 fusions go by without a rare, the 20th is rare. Nothing is ever lost or downgraded. Pairs you have never tried show only ???.    Grow, branch, and dead-end on purpose  Hatchlings gain experience in battle and glow when they are ready to evolve. Some lines branch. Some end. Then there is the altar: offer two to six Hatchlings and see how it answers. Cold, warm, hot. The right offering wakes something that is not on any chart.    Rebirth and carry one friend  Clear enough hunting grounds and you can start the village over with one Hatchling of your choice. Every rebirth opens something new.    Built to be ignored  Close the game and your village keeps going at half pace for up to 12 hours at first, and up to 24 and then 48 hours as you rebirth. Clicks pass through the empty parts of the strip. Leave your PC alone for a while and the adventurers pitch camp by the fire and keep hunting on their own, using almost no CPU. When you come back, one line tells you what they brought home.    What you get     47 species across six star tiers, including hidden ones you will only find by trying     Every Hatchling becomes a weapon in battle, enhanced up to +15, with a new look at +5 and +10     Armor and trinkets with their own stats, dropped by bosses and hunts     An equipment window and inventory to compare and break down gear     Six personalities with their own lines     A guest who visits once a day, no streaks to keep     46 Steam Achievements, a weekly boss leaderboard, Steam Cloud saves     Mornings, evenings and nights that follow your PC clock, and a winter village every December     A focus candle that turns finished sessions into eggs     Ru

about: A new Task Bar RPG — with a real economy  Task Bar Dungeons  is a new dark-fantasy idle RPG in a compact window in the corner of your screen. Three heroes fight endless hordes on their own. You pick the team, the skills and the builds — and after launch, you'll trade what you find on the Steam Community Market. We don't hunt bots. We make botting pointless.       Trading games usually lose the war against gold farms. Ours was built from day one so that farming simply doesn't pay.    Smart loot system  — keep the best, trade the rest.    No invasive anti-cheat, no random bans.     An economy that stays fair  — Steam Market trading arrives in a later update, not on launch day.    Every hero can be earned  — DLC is a shortcut, never the only way.         Everything in a DLC can also be earned in-game — through quests, crafting and secret challenges. It takes time, but everyone plays on equal terms. Buying the DLC supports us and skips the wait — with our thanks. We respect every choice. Story Mode     Yes, there are a lot of “Task Bar” games right now. That doesn't mean ours has to be empty.  We make Task Bar Dungeons because we love RPGs and idle games, and we wanted an RPG you can truly enjoy without sitting in front of the screen for hours. That's why we're actively working on a story mode: a world to dive into, heroes worth getting to know, and a plot you'll actually want to follow.   Wait, wait! If you're just here to level up and farm:  the whole story turns off with one button. Just your party and the loot.  On top of that, we'll regularly release  comics  and  interactive visual novels  about our heroes, the lore and the story. All free, simply because we love the world we've built. A new hero every month After launch we plan to add a new hero every month: new specializations, new skills, new ways to break your party build. Plays while you work Put it in the corner and get on with your day. Collapse the window to just the battle, or pin it on top. Your party fights, levels up and picks up loot on its own — even while you Alt-Tab into work — and keeps going while the game is closed, for up to 8 hours.   A meeting drags on. In the corner of your screen, Noxa pulls a whole pack of Drowned Guards into a black hole.  And if you want to go deeper… …we're not telling. Not yet. We'd rather show you on first launch. Just know this: there's more to do here than on your actual to-do list. Six heroes. Twelve ways to play. Every hero has two specializations, and one switch changes everything: weapon, skills, role in the party. Each specialization brings four skills, its own passive and its own talent tree — 15 nodes and 4 skill upgrades. Take your heroes to level 100, rebirth them for permanent bonuses and build the party nobody else thought of. A hulking werewolf, a predator's grin and weapons that match his size: when he steps forward, even the darkness gives ground. A knight of steel resolve and a steady gaze, she makes the darkest dungeon feel like a place your party can survive. Reyna turns combat into a dance along a blade's edge, with an easy smile and steel that moves faster than the eye can follow. Turn Your Desktop into an Astral Alchemy Workshop That Keeps Running    Astral Forge: Desktop Alchemist   is a living astral alchemy world designed to run beside your everyday PC use.  As you type and use your computer, you gradually gather  Stardust . These resources keep the workshop moving and prepare the way for your next alchemy experiment.  When you are busy, let it keep growing beside you.  When you have time, come back and light the forge again.     Typing → Stardust → Alchemy → Reveal → Collect                Actually Perform an Alchemy Experiment   The forge is the heart of the workshop.  Choose materials, prepare an experiment, watch the heat and changing conditions, and decide when to commit to the forge.  The result is not simply placed in front of you before the process begins.  The fun is in wondering:   What will this experiment create?   A new material, a mysterious creation, a new compendium entry, or something much rarer may be waiting after the next experiment.            Forge, Discover, Collect   Experimenting brings more materials, mysterious creations, relics, and collectibles.  Start with common discoveries, gradually fill unknown compendium entries, and keep searching for rarer results.  Growing your workshop is not just about making a number bigger.  You can actually see:   what you have discovered along the way.                The Workshop Is Not Always Quiet   An idle alchemy workshop does not stay peaceful forever.  Occasionally, workshop events appear and ask for your attention.  For example:  a dangerous bomb may suddenly show up.  Notice it early and click in time:  Defused.  Miss it and…  BOOM. about: At first, I just wanted something on my desktop to keep me company while I coded. And that’s how a little dragon that could walk around and fly across my screen came to be.  Then I thought: I spend every day reading research papers—could my dragon get stronger, too? So I gave it things to study and places to explore.  Later, I thought,   “This game is getting really fun!”   Could I share that fun with   friends  ? So dragons learned to visit each other! And  after getting judged for showing up empty-handed,  they can now bring gifts!  More and more friends were joining in! But whose dragon was stronger? Naturally, the dragons needed a way to   challenge each other  !          While exploring, I found myself with nothing much to do… so I opened a certain deckbuilding roguelike. Then I thought: why can’t my dragon play one, too?  Having two games open while sneaking in a little gaming time felt a bit risky … And that’s how   roguelike tower climbing   found its way into the Endless Tower!  One little dragon seemed a bit lonely. Could it have even littler dragons to keep it company? And so,   hatching baby dragons   became a thing! about: A desktop companion game for the corner of your screen: a hand-painted riverbank, an angler, and nine cats who get to know you, little by little.           While you're busy, there's a small riverbank in a corner of your screen, and someone sitting on it, quietly keeping you company as you work. When you're tired and look up, the water is flowing, doves lift from the bell tower, and a distant bell rings the hour. One by one, the fish go into the basket, and cats begin to come by. Nine cats who get to know you "They sat by my chair, a hand's span from my shoe, so I cast with my arm a little lower." Six cats come by the basket for fish, each with their own temper and favourite fish. One usually sits down to wash their face after eating; one sleeps so deeply that a landed fish often doesn't wake them. Three more come only in special weather. The rainy-day one wears a green cloak and carries a gourd; who comes in the snow or the heat is yours to find out. When your hand rests on a friend, they lean toward you. The name you give is the one they keep, and every first time they eat, nap or sit by the stove is kept on their page of moments.         Nothing to look after No one goes hungry or falls ill, there are no daily chores, and a cat who knows you never forgets you. While you're away, the bank carries on; when you come back, the journal tells you who came by and who slept a while in the grass. A first meeting waits until you're back. No gacha, no real-money purchases, and no cat is ever bought or sold.         Your hours, tonight's moon The light follows your computer's clock: mist in the morning, windows lighting up one by one at dusk. The church bell strikes the hour from 7 am to 10 pm and keeps quiet at night.  The moon at night is the same one outside your window; rain, snow and hot days are the riverbank's own weather. A glimpse behind the scenes: the riverbank, coming together bit by bit.         Quiet in its corner Bottom-left or bottom-right, on whichever screen you like. Three sizes; it can stay always on top, or fade while the mouse is elsewhere. When you want a clear screen, it tucks into the tray, and one click brings it back. In the corner it draws fewer frames, so it asks less of your computer. To see the cats up close, a click on the tent unrolls the whole painting.         Fishing, if you feel like it The angler fishes on their own. When the float dips, you can reel in yourself; a ★ fresh fish is the cats' favourite. After a meal, a cat leaves a few coins behind. A yellow catfish, brought up out of the water, gives a soft little croak.         Little things the cats use The cats' coins buy a cushion, a pot of wildflowers, a little tea stove. Cats rest on the cushion and warm themselves by the stove; with plants out, they come by a little more often. A cardboard box for a cat to hop into and doze in, chin on the rim, and a flat stone to nap on. On rainy days, a cat may curl up in the dry patch under the oil-paper umbrella; in the heat, one stretches out on the bamboo mat. After a sniff of catnip, some cats roll over right where they are, and when a butterfly drifts close, a cat may crouch low and watch it for a long while. The water's edge comes alive too: a kingfisher lands on the tip of the propped pole, a pair of wild ducks doze beside the raft, and at dusk or in the rain a frog hops up onto the lotus leaves.           To be clear  Nine cats, twenty kinds of fish, three rods, seventeen pieces of decor (and three more the river brings), and seventy-five first moments to come across, little by little. It's a quiet companion, not a management game: nothing to run, and no numbers to chase.   FAQ    Does the riverbank follow my weather? Rain and snow are the riverbank's own; the light follows your clock, and the moon follows the real calendar.

We wanted to find a more relaxed way to play, somewhere between exhausting micromanagement and simply waiting for progress. When life gets busy, the game needs little attention; when you have time to spare, meaningful choices and discoveries await. As you advance through the Realms and gain experience, a wider world will open before you.            If you love characters, explore their histories and relationships. If you love collecting, steadily build your trove. If you enjoy experimenting, spend your time shaping progression and assembling combat combinations.            Every new encounter and every rare find could be the beginning of your next chapter.  Practice the Arts of Cultivation, Build a Domain of Your Own  The pleasures of cultivation also lie in everyday life.       Develop your domain, grow spiritual plants, fish for spirit fish, and refine elixirs to build your sect's resources. Put the fruits of that work into character growth, equipment, and new expeditions, connecting each pursuit to the next.            Think carefully about every resource, or begin with the activities you enjoy most. Anywhere you want it, any size you want    Thin enough to sit over your taskbar — and you can put it anywhere else on screen too    You can resize it. Tuck it small into a corner, or blow it up and watch    Multiple monitors? Drag it across them    The dashboard opens only when you want it. Combat keeps going while it is closed         Melt it. about: What is AIvy?  AIvy is a desktop mascot that brings a 3D character to your PC desktop—one you can actually talk to, powered by AI. Load your favorite VRM model and watch it come to life in the corner of your screen, chatting naturally like a companion who's really there. The name comes from "AI + ivy"—the gentle vine that quietly winds itself around your everyday life.  Build Your Own Companion, Your Way  The heart of AIvy is the freedom to combine the look, the mind, the voice, and the personality—piece by piece—to craft a companion that's truly yours.  Any VRM works: one you bought on a storefront, one you built yourself in VRoid Studio, or one from VRoid Hub. VRoid Hub integration shows each model's usage terms (avatar use, modification, redistribution, commercial use) for your consent before downloading. Files can also stay where they are and be referenced without copying them into the library.  Loading a model is only the start. Swap to alternate textures bundled with the model, toggle individual parts on and off, map the model's own expressions onto AIvy's emotions, set the idle expression, and tune lighting (ambient and directional intensity, direction, color)—all saved per model. There is also a  beta feature  for outfit swapping: load .unitypackage outfit assets, the format sold on storefronts, straight onto your model (outfits authored for the same base body).  Personality and speech style can be set from ready-made presets, or written freely in your own words to shape every nuance. You can also pick how it responds—empathetic, balanced, or candid—so your companion isn't just a yes-machine.  With support for 11 languages including Japanese, English, Chinese, and Korean, people around the world can spend time with their own one-of-a-kind companion in their own language.  The Mind Runs on Your PC  For the mind, AIvy is a local LLM runner built on llama.cpp. On first launch you pick from a dropdown an open-source language model that fits your language and download it once. From then on it runs  fully offline , with no account, no API key, and no internet connection required. Your conversations are never sent anywhere.  You are not limited to the models listed in the app, either. Any GGUF file—say, one you grabbed from Hugging Face—works as AIvy's mind: pick it in settings or drop it into the models folder. There is no size cap, so a large model will run if your RAM allows.  In short, AIvy is the same kind of local LLM client as LM Studio, Jan, or GPT4All—just dressed up in a VRM character UI instead of a chat panel. The first-run download catalog is restricted to permissive licenses (Apache 2.0 / MIT) so the models are safe to use in commercial and streaming contexts.  The voice is delivered by your OS's built-in TTS. For something more characterful, there is Piper TTS: AIvy downloads and sets up both Piper itself and its voices from the settings panel, so there is  nothing to install separately . Voices are available for every supported language, and you can preview one before downloading it. If you already have VOICEVOX, AivisSpeech, Sharevox, or VoiSona Talk, you can connect those to AIvy as well.  A Quiet Presence, Designed Not to Get in the Way  AIvy isn't built to be the assistant that keeps interrupting you—it's built to be the companion whose presence you simply feel. When you're focused, it watches over you in silence. In a quieter moment, it might softly check in with "Maybe time for a break?" or "Done with that video?"—a single line that fits the situation.
